commonsForms.name: Knowledge commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared knowledge resource system whose community, rules, resource characteristics, interactions, and outcomes can be analyzed together.

commonsForms.name: Information commons
commonsForms.definition: An information resource or environment organized for shared access, use, contribution, or stewardship.

commonsForms.name: Intellectual commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared domain for the creation, exchange, and reuse of intellectual work.

commonsForms.name: Scholarly communication commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared infrastructures, norms, repositories, and publication systems for scholarly communication.

commonsForms.name: Digital commons
commonsForms.definition: A commons whose resources, access facilities, and participation are substantially digital and networked.

commonsForms.name: Open-access commons
commonsForms.definition: A knowledge commons organized around free online access and permissions broad enough for scholarly use.

commonsForms.name: Scientific or research commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared scientific literature, data, models, tools, or collaborative infrastructure supporting research.

commonsForms.name: Cultural commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared cultural works, heritage materials, archives, and the institutions or rules sustaining access to them.

commonsForms.name: Civic knowledge commons
commonsForms.definition: A participatory civic resource through which residents, students, or organizations create and use public knowledge.

commonsForms.name: Learning commons
commonsForms.definition: A shared educational environment combining information resources, technology, instruction, and collaborative learning.

commonsForms.name: Community information commons
commonsForms.definition: A community-facing information environment that supports local access, deliberation, contribution, and public problem solving.

commonsForms.name: Digital library
commonsForms.definition: A managed digital collection with discovery, access, organization, and often preservation services.

commonsForms.name: Digital archive
commonsForms.definition: A managed body of digital objects maintained across time with provenance, authenticity, or preservation responsibilities.

commonsForms.name: Institutional repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository organized by an institution to collect, expose, and often preserve its community's scholarly output.

commonsForms.name: Disciplinary repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository organized around a discipline or research community rather than one institution.

commonsForms.name: Epistemic repository
commonsForms.definition: A repository designed around a community's structured knowledge, concepts, evidence, and reusable research objects.

commonsForms.name: Specialist archive
commonsForms.definition: A focused archive built for a specialist scholarly field, corpus, format, or community.

commonsForms.name: Community-based archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive shaped and maintained with direct participation by the community represented in its holdings.

commonsForms.name: Author self-archive
commonsForms.definition: A repository or site through which authors deposit and expose their own work.

commonsForms.name: Open educational resource library
commonsForms.definition: A collection or gateway providing openly accessible teaching and learning materials.

commonsForms.name: Searchable portal
commonsForms.definition: A central discovery interface that searches or organizes resources held locally and elsewhere.

commonsForms.name: Annotated link gateway
commonsForms.definition: A link-only gateway that points to off-site resources and adds classification metadata and descriptive context.

commonsForms.name: Metadata aggregation or harvesting service
commonsForms.definition: A service that collects standardized metadata from distributed repositories to support shared discovery.

commonsForms.name: Directory or registry
commonsForms.definition: A structured listing of projects, repositories, policies, people, resources, or implementations.

commonsForms.name: Open-access journal
commonsForms.definition: A journal that makes its articles freely accessible online under an open-access delivery model.

commonsForms.name: Open publication platform
commonsForms.definition: A shared service for publishing, reviewing, distributing, or linking scholarly works outside a conventional closed journal system.

commonsForms.name: Free/libre and open-source software commons
commonsForms.definition: A software project whose code, participation rules, licenses, and collaborative production constitute a commons.

commonsForms.name: Open-content science commons
commonsForms.definition: A proposed or operating science commons applying open-source participation, review, licensing, and versioning to scientific content.

commonsForms.name: Scientific data commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared infrastructure for depositing, accessing, documenting, and reusing scientific datasets.

commonsForms.name: Collaboratory
commonsForms.definition: A networked environment in which geographically distributed participants share data, instruments, tools, and research work.

commonsForms.name: Information community
commonsForms.definition: A community joined by shared information practices, resources, tools, standards, and stewardship.

commonsForms.name: Federated or distributed library
commonsForms.definition: Multiple independent repositories or institutions connected through shared protocols, services, or discovery layers.

commonsForms.name: Coalition or membership network
commonsForms.definition: A network of institutions or projects coordinating access, policy, preservation, standards, or advocacy.

commonsForms.name: Organizational archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive housed within the same organization as either the producer or consumer, or contracted to a third party.

commonsForms.name: Producer archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive maintained by the organization or person producing the content.

commonsForms.name: Consumer archive
commonsForms.definition: An archive maintained by the institution or community consuming and relying on the content.

commonsForms.name: Independent third-party archive
commonsForms.definition: A preservation archive institutionally separate from both producer and consumer.

commonsForms.name: Distributed preservation network
commonsForms.definition: A preservation arrangement using redundant, distributed copies or caches across participating institutions.

commonsForms.name: Dark archive or fallback-access archive
commonsForms.definition: A preservation service whose stored materials become accessible only under defined loss, trigger, or continuity conditions.

commonsForms.name: Open licensing infrastructure
commonsForms.definition: Licenses, registries, declarations, or policy services that define reusable permissions for knowledge resources.

commonsForms.name: Standards and interoperability infrastructure
commonsForms.definition: Shared metadata, identifiers, protocols, interfaces, and technical rules that let independent commons interoperate.

commonsForms.name: Traditional natural-resource commons
commonsForms.definition: Shared forests, fisheries, pastures, water systems, and other subtractable resources used as the analytical starting point for knowledge commons.

commonsForms.name: Public domain
commonsForms.directoryRole: Legal status and surrounding resource pool
commonsForms.definition: Knowledge and cultural material available outside exclusive copyright control, serving as a key resource environment for commons projects.

projectTypes.name: natural-resource commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared, exhaustible natural resources provide the historical and analytic roots for knowledge-commons work.

projectTypes.name: common-pool resource
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A subtractable resource from which excluding potential beneficiaries is costly.

projectTypes.name: public good
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A generally nonrival and difficult-to-exclude good; knowledge often has these attributes.

projectTypes.name: club or toll good
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A relatively nonrival resource from which access can be excluded, including subscription systems.

projectTypes.name: private good
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A rival and excludable resource used as a contrast to commons provision.

projectTypes.name: global commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Resources and knowledge systems whose use and governance extend across political boundaries.

projectTypes.name: new commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Recently recognized shared resources, especially cultural, neighborhood, infrastructure, and knowledge resources.

projectTypes.name: knowledge commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A shared knowledge resource governed as a complex social-ecological system of artifacts, facilities, communities, and rules.

projectTypes.name: information commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared information resources or integrated campus environments combining information, technology, and assistance.

projectTypes.name: digital commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Digitally networked shared resources whose openness depends on technical and institutional design.

projectTypes.name: Internet or communication commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared communications infrastructure and participatory network space enabling decentralized exchange.

projectTypes.name: intellectual commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A domain for creating and circulating ideas through open access, custom, law, and institutional arrangements.

projectTypes.name: scholarly-communication commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared publication processes, repositories, services, and communities supporting scholarship.
representativeEntries: Workshop on Scholarly Communication as a Commons

projectTypes.name: science commons or open science
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared scientific code, models, data, literature, and collaborative infrastructure.
representativeEntries: Open Source/Content Landcover Change Modeling Effort

projectTypes.name: cultural commons and public domain
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Publicly reusable cultural materials and memory resources outside or deliberately opened beyond exclusive control.

projectTypes.name: associational commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Knowledge created through voluntary associations and civic participation.

projectTypes.name: libertarian commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Decentralized knowledge production without a single institutional manager.

projectTypes.name: commons-based peer production
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Distributed voluntary production coordinated through open networks.

projectTypes.name: participatory media commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Network platforms where users create, tag, share, and discover media.

projectTypes.name: civic or local information commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Locally grounded public knowledge built jointly by residents, students, universities, and civic organizations.

projectTypes.name: open-access commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Royalty-free scholarly literature made available online with broad reading and reuse permissions.

projectTypes.name: free, libre, and open-source software commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Source code governed through open licenses, community contribution, and project rules.

projectTypes.name: disciplinary knowledge commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared literature, tools, dialogue, and services organized around a field or research community.

projectTypes.name: research library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A library that collects, preserves, licenses, interprets, and increasingly produces scholarly resources.

projectTypes.name: public lending library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: The book's baseline access institution, governed by first sale, preservation, and public-service norms.

projectTypes.name: diffuse library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A library whose content, expertise, and access functions are distributed beyond one building or collection.

projectTypes.name: digital library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A managed digital collection joined to discovery, access, preservation, and user services.

projectTypes.name: collaborative or federated digital library
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Multiple institutions coordinate collections, protocols, and governance to provide a shared service.

projectTypes.name: digital collection
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A coherent set of digitized or born-digital objects presented as a reusable corpus.
representativeEntries: Library of Congress Edison film collection

projectTypes.name: national library and catalog
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: National-scale holdings, catalogs, and preservation coordination.

projectTypes.name: institutional repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An institutionally managed archive for faculty and organizational scholarship.

projectTypes.name: disciplinary repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A repository shared by a discipline rather than one institution.

projectTypes.name: epistemic repository
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A repository whose resource units are claims, artifacts, and community validation processes.

projectTypes.name: personal or self-archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An author's own website or deposit route for openly circulating scholarship.

projectTypes.name: organizational archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive operated by the organization that creates or controls the content; preservation Model A or B.

projectTypes.name: producer archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive run by content producers or their institutions; preservation Model C.

projectTypes.name: consumer archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive maintained by consumers or subscribing libraries; preservation Model D.

projectTypes.name: community-based or trusted third-party archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A collectively trusted independent preservation service; preservation Model E.

projectTypes.name: dark or restricted preservation archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An archive that preserves content but releases it only under specified trigger conditions.

projectTypes.name: specialist archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A narrowly focused collection assembled by a specialist or community rather than a universal institution.

projectTypes.name: web archive
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A preservation collection capturing portions of the changing web.

projectTypes.name: repository network or federation
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Interoperable repositories whose metadata and holdings form a larger distributed corpus.
representativeEntries: Networked Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations

projectTypes.name: campus information commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A shared campus facility integrating library resources, computing, consultation, and media production.

projectTypes.name: campus learning commons
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A learner-centered facility and program organized around shared learning tasks.

projectTypes.name: portal, directory, bibliography, or reference guide
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A curated discovery structure pointing users to distributed resources, policies, or concepts.

projectTypes.name: open-access journal
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A peer-reviewed journal whose articles are freely available online.

projectTypes.name: open-access publisher or journal platform
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An organization or platform that publishes and distributes OA journals.

projectTypes.name: dynamic or compound publication environment
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A publication designed for continual revision or combining journal, alerts, dialogue, data, and analytic tools.

projectTypes.name: library publishing service
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A library unit supplying publication technology, production, and stewardship.

projectTypes.name: information community
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An integrated digital setting joining a community's resources, tools, activities, and participants.
representativeEntries: University of Virginia American Studies information community

projectTypes.name: collaboratory
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An online environment for remote instrument use, data analysis, communication, and research preservation.
representativeEntries: Space Physics and Aeronomy Research Collaboratory

projectTypes.name: virtual laboratory
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A networked setting in which distributed participants configure, run, and analyze experiments.

projectTypes.name: data archive or research database
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A maintained corpus of empirical data for analysis, teaching, or civic research.

projectTypes.name: open educational resource
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Course, book, handbook, experiment, or learning content made openly usable.

projectTypes.name: civic research and mapping project
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Community-university work translating local data into public maps, indicators, deliberation, and action.

projectTypes.name: distributed preservation system
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Replicated, coordinated storage designed to keep digital materials available despite local failure.

projectTypes.name: trusted third-party preservation service
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An independent organization preserving publishers' source files under agreed access triggers.

projectTypes.name: national digital-preservation program
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A national plan or program coordinating distributed custody, standards, and stewardship.
representativeEntries: National Digital Information and Infrastructure Preservation Program

projectTypes.name: metadata-harvesting and repository interoperability protocol
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A low-barrier protocol enabling services to harvest metadata across distributed repositories.

projectTypes.name: semantic interoperability layer
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared metadata, vocabularies, and relationship structures that make heterogeneous collections work together.

projectTypes.name: repository software
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Open software for capturing, describing, exposing, and preserving repository content.

projectTypes.name: content-management and journal-workflow software
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Open software scaffolding contribution, editorial, and publication workflows.

projectTypes.name: version-control infrastructure
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Tools that track contributions, branches, and versions in distributed collaborative production.

projectTypes.name: open-source project-hosting platform
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Shared infrastructure for hosting source, versions, issue discussion, and developer coordination.

projectTypes.name: open-content license
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A standardized permission instrument allowing specified reuse of creative and knowledge works.

projectTypes.name: copyleft or open-source software license
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A license granting source access and reuse rights, sometimes requiring derivatives to remain open.

projectTypes.name: rights registry or clearance infrastructure
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Administrative machinery for registering exclusive rights or reducing permission transaction costs.

projectTypes.name: open-access declaration, mandate, or policy
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A public statement, funder rule, institutional resolution, or law establishing expectations for open dissemination.

projectTypes.name: advocacy coalition, campaign, or toolkit
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Coordinated organizations and practical resources that counter enclosure and change scholarly practice.

projectTypes.name: foundation, public trust, or funding program
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Funding and institutional sponsorship that launches, experiments with, or sustains commons infrastructure.

projectTypes.name: research-network infrastructure
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: High-capacity network services supporting distributed scholarship and collaboratories.

projectTypes.name: search, citation, and metadata-aggregation service
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A service that indexes, links, ranks, or harvests distributed knowledge resources.

projectTypes.name: mass-digitization initiative
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A program converting large cultural collections into discoverable digital form.

projectTypes.name: trusted-repository standard or audit framework
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Criteria and review structures used to establish confidence in digital repositories and preservation commitments.
representativeEntries: Task Force on Archiving of Digital Information

projectTypes.name: workshop or community of practice
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A convening that develops shared questions, practices, governance, or adoption capacity.
representativeEntries: Workshop on Scholarly Communication as a Commons

projectTypes.name: library or scholarly association
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A membership organization coordinating standards, advocacy, communities, and shared services.
representativeEntries: International Association for the Study of Common Property

projectTypes.name: civic-engagement network or campaign
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: An organization or network that connects research, teaching, public work, and community problem-solving.
representativeEntries: Campaign for the Civic Mission of Schools

projectTypes.name: glossary, handbook, and annotated-link layer
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: Interlinked definitions, explanations, experiments, readings, and external resources within a portal.

projectTypes.name: application programming interface
projectTypes.sourceGroundedScope: A language-independent interface connecting external experiment software to a commons platform.

currentStatuses.operator: Indiana University Libraries and the Ostrom Workshop, Indiana University
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The repository and its about page are online; Indiana University Libraries' 2026 guide describes it as a freely available gateway to commons literature.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same institutional repository; HTTP-era book URL is now represented by HTTPS.

currentStatuses.operator: Experimental Economics Center, Andrew Young School of Policy Studies, Georgia State University
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The economics digital library, teaching materials, and experiment services remain online.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same project at HTTPS; Georgia State's Experimental Economics Center currently links EconPort.

currentStatuses.operator: Multi-organization Conservation Commons initiative; IUCN was a participating member and signatory
currentStatuses.statusDetail: IUCN retains an official page describing its membership and the Commons principles, but no current operating project portal was verified at the book-era domain.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Use the surviving IUCN page as the current authoritative reference. Treat the book-era project domain as historical until a current operator confirms otherwise.

currentStatuses.operator: American Anthropological Association; platform hosted by Wiley
currentStatuses.statusDetail: AnthroSource is an active searchable publishing service of the American Anthropological Association on Wiley Online Library.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: The AAA-era informational URL in the book has been replaced by the Wiley-hosted service and AAA's current AnthroSource information page.

currentStatuses.operator: Alexandria Archive Institute and ArchaeoCommons; created to support the American Anthropological Association's 2004 Annual Meeting
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The surviving primary evaluation documents AnthroCommons as a virtual conference facility created for the 2004 AAA Annual Meeting; no current operating AnthroCommons site was verified.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Use the Alexandria Archive Institute evaluation as the canonical surviving project documentation, not as an active service URL.

currentStatuses.operator: arXiv, Inc.; Cornell University and the Simons Foundation are founding members during the transition
currentStatuses.statusDetail: arXiv remains active and became an independent nonprofit, arXiv, Inc., on 2026-07-01.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: The URL remains stable; organizational stewardship changed from Cornell hosting to an independent nonprofit. Earlier historical hostnames included xxx.lanl.gov.

currentStatuses.operator: DSpace community; organizational support and services provided by LYRASIS
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The open-source repository platform and community remain active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same project at HTTPS; institutional support now sits with LYRASIS rather than the book-era MIT/HP origin story.

currentStatuses.operator: Consortium Érudit: Université de Montréal, Université Laval, and Université du Québec à Montréal
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The scholarly publishing and dissemination platform remains active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same project at its current multilingual HTTPS site.

currentStatuses.operator: California Digital Library, University of California
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The University of California's open-access repository and publishing platform remains active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: The book-era California Digital Library path moved to the dedicated eScholarship domain.

currentStatuses.operator: Utrecht University Library
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The DISPUTE demonstration site evolved into the Igitur Archive and Utrecht University Repository, which is active at Utrecht's DSpace domain.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Model as historical project absorbed into Utrecht University Repository, not as an independent current service.

currentStatuses.operator: University Library, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich; original project at Washington University in St. Louis
currentStatuses.statusDetail: EconWPA stopped accepting new work in 2005; its corpus is permanently hosted as a read-only archive by LMU Munich's University Library. MPRA is the named route for new submissions.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Archive moved to LMU Munich. MPRA is explicitly identified on the archive page for new submissions: https://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/.

currentStatuses.operator: University of Oxford, Faculty of Linguistics, Philology and Phonetics; legacy service at the Bodleian Libraries
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The Bodleian OTA site remains online but stopped accepting deposits and is not updated; Oxford's Literary and Linguistic Data Service is the current access and deposit environment for the collections.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Legacy site: https://ota.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/. Current service and collections: https://llds.ling-phil.ox.ac.uk/.

currentStatuses.operator: Center for Philosophy of Science, University of Pittsburgh; official archive of the Philosophy of Science Association
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The open-access preprint archive remains active and is the official preprint archive of the Philosophy of Science Association.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same repository at HTTPS.

currentStatuses.operator: NELLCO; repository platform originally established with bepress
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The Legal Scholarship Repository's records and documents remain available on the legacy Digital Commons-style domain; NELLCO itself remains active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: No verified claim is made that NELLCO's newer Shared Repository Search replaces the Legal Scholarship Repository; record them as separate related services unless NELLCO says otherwise.

currentStatuses.bookSeed: Networked Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations (NDLTD)
currentStatuses.operator: Networked Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations
currentStatuses.statusDetail: NDLTD remains an active international organization. Its current site points users to OATD for Global ETD Search.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Organization remains at NDLTD; discovery entry point is now https://oatd.org/. The former dedicated search endpoint at https://search.ndltd.org/ was unavailable during verification.

currentStatuses.operator: ITHAKA
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The community-supported digital preservation service remains active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Same preservation service at HTTPS; Portico is identified as part of ITHAKA.

currentStatuses.operator: LOCKSS Program, Stanford Libraries
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The distributed digital preservation program remains active.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: The Stanford-hosted book-era URL moved to the dedicated lockss.org domain.

currentStatuses.operator: Institute for the Study of Knowledge Management in Education (ISKME), through OER Commons
currentStatuses.statusDetail: NSDL is available as a current OER Commons hub.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Management transferred from UCAR to ISKME in 2014; the collection now lives in OER Commons.

currentStatuses.operator: Digital Library Federation
currentStatuses.statusDetail: The Digital Library Federation preserves the project site and its 2006-2008 plans and products on its old-site domain; no current Aquifer operating service was verified.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Use the official DLF old-site copy as the archival canonical URL. American Social History Online was a principal project output/new organizational home described in the 2008 prospectus, but its present status was not asserted here.

currentStatuses.operator: Internet Archive administered the multi-organization alliance
currentStatuses.statusDetail: Internet Archive's project page describes the Open Content Alliance in the past tense as a collaborative effort; Internet Archive pages preserve the launch record and document the resulting digitization work.
currentStatuses.continuityNote: Treat OCA as a historical consortium/initiative. Its digitized outputs and related open-book work remain available through Internet Archive and Open Library; these are outputs/continuations, not asserted as a formally named successor.

stages.rule: Extract every printed link and named project; preserve spelling, page, chapter, role, and 2007 portrayal.
Resolve the book URL; find the official current page; record moves, aliases, successors, archives, status evidence, and date.
Inspect About, history, governance, host, partners, members, funders, projects, APIs, standards, preservation, and related-project pages.
Queue projects explicitly named by an official source as partners, members, successors, predecessors, spinoffs, federation members, or related commons.
Traverse official project directories, member lists, implementer registries, preservation nodes, and constituent programs.
Keep project, parent, software platform, and deployed instance distinct; preserve former names, URLs, mergers, and transfers.
Recheck URLs, redirects, status evidence, and unresolved records; add newly documented successors and partners with provenance.

expansion.breadthControl: Add a new public-facing record when an official source establishes a qualifying relationship and the entity itself offers a commons, library, directory, repository, archive, portal, journal, collaboratory, preservation network, learning commons, civic information commons, or shared knowledge infrastructure. Keep generic news, individual content items, and unrelated departments as evidence endpoints rather than projects.
